summary.text: Abraham "Abe" Hamadeh is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 8th Congressional District, elected in 2024. A former Maricopa County prosecutor and U.S. Army Reserve intelligence officer, he lost the 2022 race for Arizona Attorney General by 280 votes. He serves on the Armed Services and Veterans' Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Hamadeh was born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1991. His official bio says he was raised in Arizona's 8th District and is the son of immigrants who fled oppressive regimes in the Middle East.
He earned an undergraduate degree in political science from Arizona State University in 2012 and a J.D. from the University of Arizona College of Law in 2016.
After passing the Arizona bar in 2016 he worked as a prosecutor in the Maricopa County Attorney's Office, and according to Wikipedia he resigned in September 2021.
Hamadeh served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 2016 to 2022, reaching the rank of Captain as an intelligence officer.
In his 2022 Candidate Connection survey he described a 14-month deployment to Saudi Arabia, where he negotiated military sales and managed training for the country's domestic security forces.

Hamadeh ran for Arizona Attorney General in 2022, winning the Republican primary, and lost the general election to Democrat Kris Mayes, 1,254,809 votes to 1,254,529, a margin of 280 votes. The result went to an automatic recount, and his court challenges to it were rejected.

In October 2023, after Rep. Debbie Lesko announced her retirement, he announced a run for Arizona's 8th District. He won a crowded Republican primary and then the open seat in 2024, defeating Democrat Gregory Whitten with 56.5% of the vote on November 5.

He took office on January 3, 2025, and serves on the House Armed Services Committee, with seats on the Intelligence and Special Operations, Tactical Air and Land Forces, and Strategic Forces subcommittees. He also serves on the Veterans' Affairs Committee, with seats on its Economic Opportunity and Health subcommittees.
He advanced unopposed from the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 69,182 votes.
